chains.title: Alt T strengthens a GATA3-bound site in the TOX3 enhancer in MCF7

links.claim: The alt T allele binds GATA3 more strongly than the ref C allele in QBiC-SELEX: GATA3 has its own passing model in G010 with positive direction (GATA3 z 10.91; group effect +0.283, alt binds more). I chose GATA3 over other GATA-family members because it is by far the highest-expressed own-model member in the MCF7 expression context (346.04 TPM). E19 also shows that GATA3 ChIP-seq peaks contain this variant in MCF7, supporting occupancy, though not allele specificity.
rs4784227 lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE, EH38E3180851, with DNase and H3K27ac signal, so it is plausible that an allele-specific GATA3 site change alters enhancer activity.

TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene, 17.5 kb away, and is the best L2G gene for this variant. However, GTEx v8 shows no significant breast-mammary-tissue eQTL for this variant, so TOX3 as the direct breast target remains candidate-level rather than demonstrated.

MCF7 is the provided expression context, GATA3 is extremely highly expressed there, and GATA3 ChIP-seq peaks in MCF7 contain this variant. This supports MCF7 as a relevant cell type, although allele-specific GATA3 occupancy has not been shown.

The T allele is associated with increased breast cancer risk in GWAS and meta-analysis. The evidence does not support restricting this to ER-positive/luminal breast cancer, since ER-negative breast cancer also shows strong association.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP in MCF7 should show stronger GATA3 occupancy on the T allele than on the C allele.
Mutating the predicted GATA3 motif in an enhancer reporter should reduce the T-allele-specific enhancer effect.
If GATA3 activates TOX3, the T allele should increase TOX3 expression or enhancer activity in breast cells.
falsified_if: Existing or new MCF7 GATA3 ChIP-seq shows no allele-specific GATA3 binding at rs4784227.
GATA3 motif mutation does not affect allele-specific enhancer activity.
The T allele does not change TOX3 expression or enhancer activity in a GATA3-dependent way.

chains.title: Alt T creates a stronger MAFK site in the TOX3 enhancer, but MCF7 MAFK occupancy is unproven

links.claim: The alt T allele binds MAFK more strongly than the ref C allele in QBiC-SELEX: MAFK has its own passing model in G012 with the positive direction of the group best model. I chose MAFK over MAFG/MAFB because MAFK is the highest-expressed own-model member in the MCF7 expression context (16.96 TPM), although MAFG has the stronger individual model. This is in vitro binding only.
rs4784227 lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE, EH38E3180851, with DNase and H3K27ac signal, so an allele-specific MAFK binding change could alter enhancer activity.

TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene and the best L2G gene. However, no significant GTEx breast-mammary-tissue eQTL for this variant is reported, so a direct MAFK-to-TOX3 regulatory link in breast tissue is not demonstrated.

MAFK is expressed in the MCF7 expression context, but no ENCODE MAFK ChIP-seq peak contains this variant in MCF7; one MAFK peak contains it in HepG2. Thus MCF7 MAFK occupancy at this enhancer is plausible from expression but not supported by ChIP.
The T allele is associated with increased breast cancer risk, with very strong GWAS support and meta-analysis ORs greater than 1 for T versus C.

predictions: Allele-specific MAFK ChIP in MCF7 should show stronger MAFK occupancy on the T allele than on the C allele.
Mutating the predicted MAFK motif in an enhancer reporter should reduce the T-allele-specific enhancer effect.
If MAFK activates TOX3, the T allele should increase TOX3 expression or enhancer activity in breast cells.
falsified_if: Allele-specific MAFK ChIP in MCF7 shows no T-allele preference or no MAFK binding at the locus.
MAFK motif mutation does not affect allele-specific enhancer activity.
The T allele does not change enhancer activity or TOX3 expression in a MAFK-dependent way.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of rs4784227
predictions: No reproducible allele-specific TF binding or enhancer-activity difference should be detected for rs4784227 itself in breast cells.
The 16q12 breast cancer signal may be explained by LD with another causal variant or by a TOX3-regulatory effect not mediated by this base.
TOX3 L2G evidence may reflect locus proximity rather than a direct rs4784227 TF mechanism.
falsified_if: A reproducible allele-specific TF binding change is demonstrated at rs4784227 in a relevant breast cell type.
Allele-specific enhancer reporter activity and TOX3 expression changes are shown for this exact base.
Editing rs4784227 alone changes TOX3 expression or a breast cancer phenotype.

chains.title: Alt T loses a repressive NFATC3 site in the TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: The ref C allele binds NFATC3 more strongly than the alt T allele in QBiC-SELEX: NFATC3 has an own passing model in G026 with negative direction, but its model barely passes the gate and the group best model is NFATC4. I chose NFATC3 because it is the highest-expressed own-model member in MCF7 (9.54 TPM). No allele-specific ChIP evidence is available.
The variant lies in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE, so loss of a repressive NFATC3 site could in principle change enhancer output.
TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene and best L2G gene, but no significant breast GTEx eQTL is reported, so TOX3 as the target of an NFATC3-dependent effect is not demonstrated.
NFATC3 is expressed in the provided MCF7 context, but there is no MCF7 ChIP evidence that NFATC3 binds this enhancer.

The T allele is the breast cancer risk allele, but the mechanistic claim that loss of a repressive NFATC3 site increases TOX3 and thereby contributes to risk rests on an untested repression assumption.

predictions: Allele-specific NFATC3 ChIP should show stronger NFATC3 binding on the C allele and reduced binding on the T allele.
If NFATC3 represses TOX3, NFATC3 knockdown should increase TOX3 expression or enhancer activity.
Mutating the predicted NFATC3 motif should phenocopy the T allele in an enhancer reporter.
falsified_if: NFATC3 does not bind this locus allele-specifically in breast cells.
The T allele does not reduce NFATC3 occupancy.
NFATC3 knockdown does not change TOX3 expression or enhancer activity in the predicted direction.

grades_v0.reason: The QBiC-SELEX data show an allele-specific in vitro binding change for MAFK (E08, G012, MAFK own model, z 48.84, effect +2.788, alt binds more). This is direct for the in vitro model, but the instructions treat a QBiC-SELEX binding change alone as at best weak support for a binding link. There is no allele-specific ChIP, reporter, MPRA, or other perturbation evidence at this variant. The choice of MAFK over MAFG is at least justified by expression (MAFK 16.96 TPM vs MAFG 8.48 TPM in the provided context), although MAFG has the stronger model.

E01 places the variant in ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer and E03 places it in dELS EH38E3180851 with DNase and H3K27ac signal. This directly supports the element-location part of the claim. Caveat: E03 gives maxima across ENCODE biosamples, not MCF7-specific activity.

E02 shows TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene at 17.5 kb; E05 shows TOX3 as the best L2G gene (0.92-0.96); E06a describes rs4784227 as a TOX3 enhancer mutation. This is supportive but not a breast-tissue colocalising eQTL or perturbation experiment. The TOX3 eQTL credible sets in E05 are brain and low PIP. Thus TOX3 is the best candidate target but not directly demonstrated.

E07 defines MCF7/ACH-000019 as the expression context, and E08 shows MAFK expression there. However, E03 does not provide MCF7-specific chromatin or ChIP evidence that this enhancer is active and MAFK-bound in MCF7. The cell-type plausibility is therefore indirect.

E04 reports breast cancer association with effect allele T at p 2.0e-240, and E06b reports meta-analysis ORs >1 for T versus C (OR 1.244) and TT versus CC (OR 1.544). The direction is consistent with the alt T being the risk allele.

E17 shows GATA3 has an own passing QBiC-SELEX model in G010 with positive effect (GATA3 z 10.91; group best GATA2 z 18.65; effect +0.283, alt binds more). This supports only an in vitro binding change and is weak for an in-cell binding link. GATA3 is extremely highly expressed in the provided context (346.04 TPM), which justifies choosing it over lower-expressed GATA family members, but no GATA3 ChIP or allele-specific assay is cited.
E01 and E03 directly place the variant in an enhancer/dELS with active chromatin marks. As above, the chromatin data are not MCF7-specific in this call.

TOX3 is the nearest gene (E02) and the strongest L2G target (E05), but this is not a breast-specific colocalising eQTL or an experimental target-gene demonstration. E05's TOX3 eQTL credible sets are brain and low PIP. The gene link is plausible but indirect.

E17 shows GATA3 is highly expressed in the provided MCF7 expression context, and GATA3 is a plausible luminal breast TF, but there is no MCF7-specific GATA3 ChIP or chromatin evidence at this cCRE. Expression alone does not establish that this enhancer is GATA3-responsive in MCF7.

The general claim that T increases breast cancer risk is supported by E04 and E06b. However, the added claim that this is 'especially in ER-positive/luminal breast cancer' is overclaimed: E04 also shows a stronger ER-negative association (p 2.0e-26) than ER-positive (p 1.0e-13), and luminal A appears only as an L2G credible set, not as an allele-specific phenotype in the cited evidence.

E11 shows NFATC3 has an own passing QBiC-SELEX model in G026 with negative direction (NFATC3 z -4.28; group best NFATC4 z -23.46; effect -1.044, alt binds less). This supports a weak in vitro ref-allele-preferring binding change. NFATC3 was chosen as the highest-expressed own-model member (9.54 TPM), but its model barely passes the gate and the group's best model is NFATC4. No allele-specific ChIP or reporter evidence is cited.
E01 and E03 directly place the variant in an enhancer/dELS with active chromatin marks. The functional consequence of losing a TF site is not directly tested.

TOX3 is the nearest gene and the best L2G target (E02, E05), but there is no breast eQTL/colocalisation or perturbation evidence proving TOX3 as the target of this exact base. The gene assignment is candidate-level.

E11 shows NFATC3 expression in the provided MCF7 context, but there is no MCF7-specific evidence that NFATC3 binds or regulates this enhancer. The cell-type link rests on expression plus in vitro motif prediction.

E04 and E06b support T as the breast cancer risk allele. However, the mechanistic claim that loss of a repressive NFATC3 site on T increases TOX3 and thereby contributes to risk is not supported by the cited evidence; there is no evidence cited that NFATC3 represses TOX3. The phenotype direction is consistent only under an untested repression assumption.

grades_final.reason: E17 shows GATA3 has its own passing QBiC-SELEX model in G010 with positive group direction (alt binds more), and E19 shows GATA3 ChIP-seq peaks in MCF7 contain the variant. However, E19 does not show allele specificity, so the allele-specific binding claim rests on QBiC-SELEX alone, which is at best weak support for occupancy in cells.
E01 and E03 directly place rs4784227 in an enhancer-like cCRE/dELS with DNase and H3K27ac signal. This supports enhancer localization, although allele-specific enhancer activity is not tested.

E02 and E05 support TOX3 as the nearest protein-coding gene and best L2G candidate, but E18 reports no significant GTEx breast-mammary-tissue eQTL. No perturbation or allele-specific reporter links this variant to TOX3, so the gene link remains candidate-level only.

E17 shows very high GATA3 expression in the MCF7 expression context, and E19 shows GATA3 ChIP-seq peaks containing this variant in MCF7. This supports MCF7 relevance for GATA3 occupancy, though not allele-specific occupancy.

E04 and E06b support the T allele as the breast cancer risk allele, including strong ER-negative as well as ER-positive associations. One E04 row lists C as the effect allele for a breast-cancer-related trait, which is a direction inconsistency worth flagging, but the dominant breast cancer and meta-analysis evidence is T-risk.

E08 shows MAFK has its own passing QBiC-SELEX model in G012 and follows the group positive direction (alt binds more), and the MAFK-over-MAFG choice is justified by higher MCF7 expression. But this is QBiC-SELEX in vitro binding only; E20 provides no MCF7 MAFK ChIP support at the locus.

E01 and E03 directly place the variant in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal. The element context is supported, but an allele-specific enhancer-activity effect is not demonstrated.

E02 and E05 support TOX3 as nearest gene and best L2G candidate, and E06a is a review mentioning rs4784227 in a TOX3/enhancer context. E18 shows no breast GTEx eQTL, and no MAFK perturbation links this variant to TOX3, so the gene link is not demonstrated.

E08 supports MAFK expression in the MCF7 context, and E20 reports no MCF7 MAFK ChIP peak containing the variant, with one HepG2 peak. This is consistent with unproven MCF7 occupancy, but E20 absence can reflect lack of experiment and does not establish non-occupancy.

E04 and E06b support the T allele as associated with increased breast cancer risk, with ORs >1 for T versus C in meta-analysis. The same caveat about one E04 row listing C as effect allele applies, but the overall T-risk direction is supported.

E11 shows NFATC3 is an own-model member of G026 and is a passing member with negative direction, but its z-score is only -4.28, barely passing the gate, and the group best model is NFATC4. No allele-specific ChIP or reporter supports NFATC3 binding, so this is weak QBiC-SELEX-only evidence.
E01 and E03 directly show the variant lies in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE. This supports the element context, but does not show that NFATC3 site loss changes enhancer output.

E02 and E05 support TOX3 proximity and L2G, but E18 shows no significant breast GTEx eQTL, and there is no NFATC3 perturbation or allele-specific reporter linking the variant to TOX3. The TOX3 target remains candidate-level.

E11 supports NFATC3 expression in the MCF7 expression context, but the claim that there is no MCF7 ChIP evidence is an absence not documented by a cited NFATC3 Factorbook/ENCODE lookup. Cell-type relevance is expression-based only.

E04 and E06b support the T allele as the breast cancer risk allele, but the mechanistic phenotype claim depends on the untested assumption that NFATC3 is repressive at this enhancer and that its loss increases TOX3. The genetic association is supported; the repressive-loss mechanism is not.

checks.why: This would directly test whether TOX3 is the target of rs4784227 in breast tissue, affecting the gene link in all three non-null chains.

GATA3 is the most highly expressed candidate TF in the provided context; an ENCODE/Factorbook GATA3 peak overlapping this variant in MCF7 would substantially strengthen H2 and could make it competitive with H1.

H1 is currently the highest-probability chain, and its main weakness is that MAFK binding is only predicted in vitro. A MAFK ChIP peak containing this variant in MCF7 would strongly support the binding/cell-type links; absence would weaken H1.

The pooled ORs regarding the association between the rs4784227-CASC16 polymorphism and breast cancer risk were statistically significant [T vs C: OR = 1.244, 95% CI = 1.202-1.287; TT vs CT + CC: OR = 1.407, 95% CI = 1.296-1.528; CC vs CT + TT: OR = 0.777, 95% CI = 0.745-0.811; TT vs CC: OR = 1.544, 95% CI = 1.419-1.681; CT vs CC: OR = 1.244, 95% CI = 1.189-1.301].

Our pooled analysis showed a significant association between the rs4784227- (T) allele and breast cancer susceptibility in Asian and North American populations, and intervention with this mutation might be a new therapeutic strategy for breast cancer.
